1. Claim 4 (Currently Amended): A method of impeding Leishmania transmission in humans by immunizing a canine animal with a composition comprising a Fucose Mannose Ligand (FML) fraction from Leishmania promastigotes or Leishmania amastigotes and saponin, wherein antibodies generated in the immunized canine animal reduce the parasitic load available to sandflies, thereby reducing human incidence of Leishmaniasis.

2. Claim 5 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 4 wherein said composition is in the form of a blocking vaccine comprising the FML fraction and saponin.

3. Claim 6 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 4 wherein said composition further comprises suitable pharmacological vehicles, for blocking Leishmaniasis transmission in humans through reduction of parasitic transmission from canine vectors to sandflies.

4. Claim 7 (Currently Amended): The method of claim 4 wherein the Leishmania promastigotes or Leishmania amastigotes fractions called "Fucose Mannose Ligand" (FML) comprise a glycoprotein complex containing 29% of neutral sugar, 44% of protein, 11% of phosphate and hexoamines traces composed by protein bands with molecular weight ranging from 9 to 95 kDa, some protein bands having carbohydrates at 36 and 54 to 68 kDa, the FML glycidic portion presenting 10% of fucose and 47% of mannose, 30% of glucose, 12% of galactose and xylose traces, amino acids containing 10 to 20% of glutamic acid, alanine, aspartic acid and glycine, 5 to 10% of serine, histidine, lysine, leucine, threonine, proline and valine, and 2 to 5% of arginine, methionine, isoleucine, tyrosine and phenylalanine, wherein the method achieves blocking of Leishmaniasis transmission in humans through immunization of canine animals.
